newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's left takes ruling party to court.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's left takes ruling party to court.

text.p: Mexico's main leftist opposition party on Monday filed suit against the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) on charges of using public funds to win votes.

The Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) said in a statement it filed charges at the Attorney General's Office against the PRI gubernatorial candidate and a handful of other PRI officials in the eastern state of Campeche.
The PRD alleged the PRI handed out free parcels of publicly funded medicine in the state as if they were donations from President Ernesto Zedillo's party.

Campeche is one of six Mexican states where elections are scheduled to take place in July. Mexico City residents will vote for their first-ever mayor and most of the country's Congress is also up for grabs.
The PRD said Mexico's health laws prohibited anyone from tampering with public medicines and said they faced up to nine years in prison if found guilty.
The PRI, which has held the presidency, control of Congress and most state governorships for 68 consecutive years, has denied misusing state resources for electoral purposes.
